cohort: 112 pregnant women (66 morbidly obese and 46 super-obese) at Tygerberg Hospital, South Africa.
finding: Super-obese women experience higher rates of pre-eclampsia, intrauterine growth restriction, surgical complications and prolonged hospital stay compared to morbidly obese women.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were high in both groups (54% in super-obese, 41% in morbidly obese) but this difference was not statistically significant.
